existing_invitation_flow.token_identity: The raw invitation token is 32 random bytes, hex-encoded, generated server-side at lib/invitations/service.ts:66; only its SHA-256 (lib/invitations/service.ts:35-37,67) is persisted, in invitations.tokenHash (db/schema.ts:145). The raw token exists only in the HTTP response of the create call and in the email body — never in a durable row.
existing_invitation_flow.consequence_for_resend: Because the raw token cannot be reconstructed from tokenHash, any resend that must produce a working accept link again has exactly two options: (a) rotate — mint a new raw token, persist its new hash, invalidate the old one, or (b) additionally persist the raw token (plaintext or reversibly encrypted) so it can be re-emitted. HPO-C selects (a) explicitly and forbids (b) explicitly ('raw invitation token must NOT be stored encrypted for resend'). This authority treats that selection as settled, not as an open design question.
existing_invitation_flow.commit_before_send_already_implemented: app/app/organization/members/actions.ts:36-42 already implements 'commit before send' for the CURRENT invitation flow: createInvitation() runs inside withOrganizationDatabaseContext (db/identity-context.ts) — a real db.transaction — and returns a `sendEmail` closure without invoking it; the closure is invoked at actions.ts:42, strictly after the transaction that persisted the invitation and its INVITATION_SENT audit row has returned (committed). The in-code comment at actions.ts:37-38 and the module header at lib/invitations/service.ts:1-11 both state the reasoning this authority now generalizes: a token emailed inside an open transaction that then rolls back would be a live link resolving to nothing.
existing_invitation_flow.audit_ordering: logAuditAction(AUDIT_ACTIONS.INVITATION_SENT) is called at lib/invitations/service.ts:83-90, INSIDE createInvitation, which itself runs inside the withOrganizationDatabaseContext transaction opened by the caller (actions.ts:39-41). So INVITATION_SENT is committed to audit_logs together with the invitations row, BEFORE the provider is ever called. It records that a send was ATTEMPTED-TO-BE-ATTEMPTED, not that a send succeeded, and its afterJson (service.ts:89) carries no delivery outcome. This is exactly the reconciliation problem: introducing email_deliveries must not touch AUDIT_ACTIONS.INVITATION_SENT's meaning or timing, which is authorized, correct, and orthogonal to delivery — see email_delivery_model.audit_relationship below.

HPO-ASY-01.title: SCOPE — one table, no queue platform, no generalization
HPO-ASY-01.disposition: email_deliveries is authorized as a single, purpose-built table for Resend-backed notification sends (invitation email today; demo-request notification per HPO-ASY-10). It is NOT a queue, NOT a job table, and carries NO `kind`/`payload` polymorphism that would let an unrelated future notification type be bolted on without its own HPO review. stripe_webhook_events and operation_tickets are reconciled as PATTERN references only (reconciled_current_state above) and are not modified, extended, or merged.

HPO-ASY-02.title: Email delivery identity and idempotency
HPO-ASY-02.disposition: Identity is SERVER-ISSUED at row-creation time and IS the idempotency boundary, mirroring the argument in operation_tickets (`reconciled_current_state.operation_tickets`) and the mechanism in stripe_webhook_events (`event_id` as PRIMARY KEY). email_deliveries.id (a server-generated UUID or an opaque digest of two independent random UUIDs, in the style of INT-INT-001 §5's ticket_id — the exact form is an implementation-time choice, not fixed here) is the PRIMARY KEY and the ONLY idempotency key: it is never derived from message content, recipient address, or invitation id, because a derived key would let two logically distinct send attempts (e.g. the original send and a rotated resend) collide or, conversely, would let a client-controlled retry of the identical logical attempt mint a second row. A manual RETRY of an existing attempt (HPO-ASY-08) re-uses the SAME row id and transitions its state; a RESEND (HPO-ASY-05) is a logically NEW attempt bound to a NEW invitation token and therefore gets a NEW email_deliveries row — it is never modeled as a retry of the old one.
closed_field_list_minimum: reference_type (closed vocabulary, e.g. 'invitation' | 'demo_request' — NOT free text)
reference_id (the invitations.id or demo_requests.id this delivery is FOR)
status (CHECK, exactly the five HPO-C states)
attempts (integer, counts manual attempts only — never incremented by anything automatic)
last_error_code (CHECK, closed vocabulary, NOT the provider's free-text message — see pii_minimization)
queued_at / accepted_at / failed_at / cancelled_at (nullable timestamps, at most one of accepted_at/failed_at/cancelled_at ever set, matching stripe_webhook_events' completed_at/failed_at split)

HPO-ASY-03.title: Transaction boundary
HPO-ASY-03.disposition: The email_deliveries row is created in status='queued' inside the SAME database transaction that persists the referenced business row (the invitations insert, or — per HPO-ASY-10 — the demo_requests insert) and its audit entry. This generalizes the EXISTING, already-correct pattern at app/app/organization/members/actions.ts:36-42 / lib/invitations/service.ts:70-90 rather than introducing a new one. The provider.send() call happens STRICTLY AFTER that transaction has returned (committed) — never inside it, and never inside any transaction at all. A resend (HPO-ASY-05) follows the same rule: the new invitations token-rotation UPDATE, the new email_deliveries 'queued' row, and the cancellation of the superseded email_deliveries row are one transaction; the new provider.send() call happens after it commits.
HPO-ASY-03.explicit_negative: A transaction is never held open across a provider network call. This is not a performance preference; it is the same correctness argument already recorded in the current code (a token/business row that commits and then a provider call that stalls holding row locks is the exact hazard actions.ts:36-38's comment names).

HPO-ASY-04.title: Provider attempt semantics and result categories
HPO-ASY-04.disposition: Exactly ONE provider.send() call is made per manual attempt (initial create, or an explicit manual retry/resend). The result of that single call is classified into exactly one of the five HPO-C states before the function returns control to its caller — never left as an untyped null the way resend-client.ts:24,39 and lib/invitations/email.ts:44-46 do today.

result_categories.queued: The email_deliveries row exists and no provider call has yet been attempted, or an attempt is about to be made. This is the state the row is created in, inside the transaction (HPO-ASY-03).
result_categories.accepted: The provider call returned successfully (a message id was returned, matching the `data.id` branch at resend-client.ts:42). This means the PROVIDER ACCEPTED THE MESSAGE FOR DELIVERY. It is a terminal-for-this-attempt state but it is explicitly NOT a claim of delivery, bounce-free receipt, or the recipient having seen the message (see accepted_never_means_delivered).
result_categories.failed_retryable: The provider call failed in a way a human-initiated retry could plausibly succeed at (e.g. a transient network/5xx condition, a rate limit, a temporary provider-side error). Classification detail (which Resend error shapes map here) is an implementation-time decision against the pinned SDK version, not fixed by this authority — but the row MUST carry a closed-vocabulary last_error_code, never the raw SDK error text (pii_minimization).
result_categories.failed_permanent: The provider call failed in a way no retry of the SAME message will fix (e.g. a malformed/rejected recipient address, a policy rejection). A failed_permanent invitation delivery does not block a RESEND once the operator changes something material (typically nothing changes for an invitation resend except the token — if the recipient address itself was the defect, the underlying invitation must be revoked and re-created, which is out of scope for the delivery ledger to decide).
result_categories.cancelled: The row was superseded before (or without) a terminal provider outcome — the only two authorized triggers are a resend (HPO-ASY-05, the OLD delivery for a rotated token is cancelled) and a revoke (revokeInvitation already exists at lib/invitations/service.ts:119-151; a queued/accepted delivery for a revoked invitation is cancelled, never fired at nor left dangling).

HPO-ASY-04.accepted_never_means_delivered: Restated because HPO-C is explicit and this is the state most likely to be misread in a UI: 'accepted' records that Resend's API returned success for the send call. It carries NO information about bounce, spam-folder placement, or the recipient opening the message. No UI text, audit action name, or variable name introduced under this authority may use the word 'delivered' for this state.

HPO-ASY-05.title: Resend / token-rotation semantics
HPO-ASY-05.disposition: A manual 'Resend' action on a pending invitation (i) generates a NEW raw token exactly as createInvitation does today (lib/invitations/service.ts:66-67), (ii) UPDATEs the SAME invitations row's tokenHash and expiresAt to the new values (the invitation's identity — id, email, role — does not change; only its credential does), (iii) transitions any prior email_deliveries row for that invitation that is still in 'queued' or 'accepted' to 'cancelled' (a stale accepted delivery pointed a working link at a now-invalidated token hash — leaving it 'accepted' would be a lie about what that link now does), and (iv) creates a NEW email_deliveries row in 'queued', bound to the SAME invitation reference_id, in the SAME transaction as (ii) and (iii). The provider send for the new token happens after that transaction commits (HPO-ASY-03). Because the raw token is only ever transient (existing_invitation_flow.token_identity), rotation is not a workaround for an inability to resend the old link — it is the ONLY mechanism that can produce a working link a second time, which is exactly why HPO-C forbids the alternative (encrypting the raw token at rest) rather than merely declining to require it: that alternative is a materially larger PII/secret-custody surface for a capability rotation already satisfies for free.
HPO-ASY-05.explicit_prohibition: No column anywhere (invitations, email_deliveries, or any future table) may store the raw token in a form recoverable by the application — hashed-only remains the sole persisted form, unchanged from today's schema (db/schema.ts:145).

HPO-ASY-06.title: PII minimization
HPO-ASY-06.disposition: email_deliveries follows stripe_webhook_events' discipline exactly (reconciled_current_state.stripe_webhook_specialized_ledger): NO payload column, ever. Specifically: (a) no email HTML/body is persisted — the template is regenerable from the referenced invitation/demo_request row plus the (already-existing) template functions, so persisting a rendered copy would be a second, driftable copy of the same PII for no operational gain; (b) no raw provider response is persisted, only the closed-vocabulary last_error_code (HPO-ASY-02); (c) the recipient email address is NOT duplicated onto email_deliveries — it is reached via reference_id -> invitations.email (or -> demo_requests.email per HPO-ASY-10), so there is exactly one durable copy of the address, not two that can diverge; (d) attempts is a count, never a log of each attempt's raw error text.
HPO-ASY-06.retention: Explicitly NOT decided here. HPO-C is unambiguous: 'Retention/PII duration remains governed by HPO-F/legal review; do not invent number of days.' This authority defines NO default TTL, NO cron-based purge, and NO column implying one (e.g. no `purge_after` default value). A successor lane may add a nullable retention marker only once HPO-F fixes a number; inventing a placeholder number now would itself be the prohibited act.

HPO-ASY-07.title: UI-visible semantics
HPO-ASY-07.disposition: The organization members UI (app/app/organization/members/**, currently rendering only invitations.status: pending/accepted/revoked/expired) is authorized to additionally surface email_deliveries.status per pending invitation, as a SEPARATE, clearly-labeled field — never merged into or overwritten by invitations.status, since the two answer different questions (has the invite been accepted vs did the email get to the provider). Required UI vocabulary: 'queued' MAY render as 'Enviando…'/'Sending…'; 'accepted' MUST render as language equivalent to 'Sent' or 'Accepted by provider' and MUST NOT render as 'Delivered' or imply the recipient received it (HPO-ASY-04.accepted_never_means_delivered); 'failed_retryable' and 'failed_permanent' MUST both surface a visible 'Resend' affordance (HPO-ASY-08 governs who may click it); 'cancelled' MAY be hidden from the default view (it is superseded, not actionable) but MUST remain queryable for support/audit. This closes the specific defect LANE F16's census recorded (a prior independent measurement, corroborated not re-verified here) that invitation confirmations are otherwise invisible in this UI.

HPO-ASY-08.title: Manual retry authorization
HPO-ASY-08.disposition: A manual retry (re-attempting the SAME email_deliveries row, e.g. after failed_retryable) or a resend (HPO-ASY-05, a new row) is authorized under the EXACT SAME actor and tenancy boundary as the existing invite/revoke actions: `canInviteUsers(membership.role)` (lib/invitations/service.ts:42,121) gates the action, and the acting organization's id MUST equal the referenced invitation's organizationId (mirroring revokeInvitation's explicit cross-org check, lib/invitations/service.ts:131, 'if (invitation.organizationId !== ctx.organization.id) throw new Error("Forbidden")'). No lesser role, and no actor from a different organization even holding a valid session, may retry or resend a delivery belonging to another organization's invitation. This is a negative control this authority requires be tested (see companion manifest, cross-org authorization).

HPO-ASY-09.title: erasure_partial recovery semantics
HPO-ASY-09.disposition: The terminal guard at lib/pipeline/evidence.ts:948 is authorized to be narrowed so that erasure_partial no longer blocks re-entry into requestGovernedEvidenceErasure for the SAME evidence item, while erasure_complete continues to block it exactly as today. The retry MUST reuse the existing versionsToSweep filter (evidence.ts:954, already excludes erasure_complete versions) unchanged — a retry only ever re-attempts versions that are NOT already at the terminal complete state, never all versions unconditionally. The three-step sequence (durable erasure_requested write FIRST, then the external/content operation, then the durable terminal/partial write) is unchanged and applies identically on retry. A NEW governed audit verb is authorized for this specific transition — 'evidence_tombstone.erasure_retry_requested' — logged the same way and at the same point AC-1 logs 'erasure_requested' today (evidence.ts comment block, lines 913-925), so a retry is auditably distinguishable from a first attempt rather than silently re-emitting the same verb. erasure_blocked is unaffected: it remains unreachable at this stage exactly as documented (evidence.ts comment, lines 927-934) and this authority does not activate it.
HPO-ASY-09.explicit_non_goal: This is a state-machine correction, not a durability/queue mechanism. Re-sweeping remains a SYNCHRONOUS, manually-triggered call — the same shape as today's single call — not a background retry loop. No automatic re-sweep is authorized (consistent with HPO-C's 'no automatic retry/cron is required for V1').

HPO-ASY-10.title: Demo persistence semantics
HPO-ASY-10.disposition: submitDemoRequest (app/actions/marketing/demo-request.ts) is authorized to gain exactly one new durable row per submission, written BEFORE the notification email is attempted (the REVERSE order-of-priority from the invitation flow, and deliberately so: here the demo request itself — not a delivery record about it — is the business fact HPO-C requires survive a provider outage). Minimum column set, mirroring the PII-minimization discipline of HPO-ASY-06: id, name, organization (free text as submitted), email, message (nullable, as submitted), ip (already collected at demo-request.ts:41-45, for rate-limit correlation — retained at the same minimization level already in force, not expanded), created_at. This is a NEW table (name not fixed here — NOT `marketing_leads`, per reconciled_current_state.marketing_leads_and_demo's explicit disambiguation of the two features) or, if a successor lane finds it materially simpler, a narrowly-scoped `reference_type='demo_request'` row referenced by an email_deliveries entry the same way an invitation is — that choice is left open for implementation, but creating NO row at all is no longer authorized. The honeypot short-circuit (demo-request.ts:58-61, silently returns ok without sending or persisting) is UNCHANGED: a tripped honeypot must continue to produce zero durable trace, since it is deliberately not a real submission. The existing in-memory per-IP rate limit (lib/marketing/demo-request-rate-limit.ts) is UNCHANGED and out of scope — HPO-C does not ask for durable rate limiting, and generalizing it is exactly the scope creep §1 of this authority forbids.
HPO-ASY-10.notification_send_relationship: The notification email to hola@uellix.com MAY still be attempted synchronously in the same request, after the demo_request row commits, and MAY reuse the same email_deliveries table (reference_type='demo_request') for its own queued/accepted/failed_retryable/failed_permanent/cancelled tracking — but a failure of that send MUST NOT cause the demo_requests row itself to be rolled back or deleted; the two are governed by the transaction boundary rule (HPO-ASY-03) exactly as invitations are, with the demo_requests insert playing the role invitations.insert plays today.

email_delivery_model.state_diagram: queued -[provider call succeeds]-> accepted (terminal-for-attempt) ; queued -[provider call fails, retryable]-> failed_retryable -[manual retry]-> queued ; queued -[provider call fails, permanent]-> failed_permanent (terminal, no auto-retry; a resend creates a NEW row instead of transitioning this one) ; {queued|accepted} -[superseded by resend or by invitation revoke]-> cancelled (terminal)
email_delivery_model.no_state_named_delivered: Deliberate. 'delivered'/'bounced'/'opened' would require a provider webhook (Resend delivery events) this authority does not authorize wiring — see out_of_scope.
email_delivery_model.audit_relationship: email_deliveries is a STATE ledger, not a replacement for audit_logs. AUDIT_ACTIONS.INVITATION_SENT keeps its current meaning and timing exactly (reconciled_current_state.invitation_sent_audit_ordering). New audit verbs authorized for governed vocabulary, to be added to lib/audit/logger.ts's AUDIT_ACTIONS map by a successor lane (not created by this artifact): 'email_delivery.accepted', 'email_delivery.failed_retryable', 'email_delivery.failed_permanent', 'email_delivery.cancelled', 'email_delivery.resend_requested' (HPO-ASY-05), 'email_delivery.retry_requested' (HPO-ASY-08), 'evidence_tombstone.erasure_retry_requested' (HPO-ASY-09), 'demo_request.received' (HPO-ASY-10). A successor lane MUST use these exact literal strings rather than inventing alternatives, so this authority's naming is the single source of truth for the vocabulary, not a suggestion re-derived per implementer.

out_of_scope: A general async job/queue/outbox table serving more than one notification kind (HPO-ASY-01).

Any scheduler, cron job, or background worker — pg_cron is not installed in this project's baseline (LANE F12 measurement, corroborated by INT-INT-001 §4 independently) and this authority does not propose installing one.
Resend delivery-event webhooks (bounce/open/click tracking) and any 'delivered' state derived from them.
Hosted Resend configuration of any kind (API key provisioning, sending domain, DNS records).
Unifying stripe_webhook_events and email_deliveries under one table, one set of functions, or one migration file (HPO-C explicit prohibition).
Generalizing marketing_leads / CAP-04 or wiring its unapplied `submit_lead` definer — untouched, per reconciled_current_state.marketing_leads_and_demo.
Fixing the CAP-03/CAP-04 RLS/definer gaps noted in reconciled_current_state — those belong to their own capability lanes, not this one.
Deciding or defaulting a PII retention/purge duration for email_deliveries or demo_requests (HPO-ASY-06 — HPO-F/legal owns this).
Any change to AUDIT_ACTIONS.INVITATION_SENT's timing, meaning, or afterJson shape.
Any change to operation_tickets (INT-INT-001) — cited as pattern precedent only.
